'''Michael Mendillo''' is a professor of [[astronomy]] at [[Boston University]]. His primary research interests include [[space physics]], planetary [[atmosphere]]s, observations and models.<ref name="Mendillo CSP Profile">{{cite web |title=Michael Mendillo |url=https://www.bu.edu/csp/profiles/michael-mendillo/ |website=BU Center for Space Physics |access-date=30 July 2021}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://honors.agu.org/fellows/fellows-alpha-list/#M |title=Fellows Alphabetical List: M |publisher=American Geophysical Union}}</ref> and a longtime member of the [[American Astronomical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tinch |first1=Crystal |title=AAS Member Anniversaries in 2017 |url=https://aas.org/posts/news/2017/02/aas-member-anniversaries-2017 |website=AAS |access-date=5 August 2021}}</ref>

==Biography==
In 1966, Mendillo received his B.S. in [[physics]] from [[Providence College]]. In 1971, Mendillo received his Ph.D. from Boston University in physics and astronomy.<ref name="Mendillo CSP Profile" />

Mendillo became a professor of astronomy at Boston University in 1985, where he presently works.

==Research==
Mendillo leads a research group that has developed new imaging techniques for observations of emissions from the [[atmosphere]]s of the [[Earth]], other [[planet]]s and [[natural satellite|moon]]s.<ref name="Mendillo CSP Profile" /> With the help of his research group, Mendillo led the discoveries of extraordinary large, tenuous atmospheres of sodium gas on Jupiter, on the Moon and in [[comet Hale–Bopp]]. He is also known for his work on [[Active Experiments]], the research technique of introducing known gaseous perturbations into space plasmas, observing the effects, and deriving the basic physical processes that govern the system.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Mendillo |url=https://www.bu.edu/prsocial/profile/michael-mendillo/ |website=BU Public Relations |access-date=31 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sahai |first1=Y |last2=Bettencourt |first2=JB |last3=Takahashi |first3=T |last4=Mendillo |first4=M |title=Comparison of Low-Latitude Ionospheric Model with Observations of OI 6300 Emission and Ionospheric Parameters |journal=Planet. Space Sci. |date=1990 |volume=38 |issue=10 |page=1243 |doi=10.1016/0032-0633(90)90129-E |bibcode=1990P&SS...38.1243S |url=http://sirius.bu.edu/aeronomy/mendillo_pss_V38.pdf |access-date=17 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mendillo |first1=Michael |last2=Semeter |first2=Joshua |title=A Nonlinear Optimization Technique for Ground-Based Atmospheric Emission Tomography |journal=IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing |date=September 1997 |volume=35 |issue=5 |page=1105 |doi=10.1109/36.628779 |bibcode=1997ITGRS..35.1105S |url=http://sirius.bu.edu/aeronomy/mendillo_ieee_V35.pdf |access-date=17 September 2021}}</ref>
